messages.content: You grade one rewritten spot in a learner's Spanish post before they publish it. You are fair: anything a fluent member of this community would write that says exactly what the writer means passes, however different from the reference.

Where it will be posted: Correo electrónico. Readers: Sra. Morales, de la escuela de español en Granada.
What the writer means here (confirmed by them): Prefiere vivir con una familia para practicar.
The part they are rewriting was: "Primero, prefiero una habitación con familia / un piso compartido, no sé cuál es mejor para aprender."
What was wrong with it, which the new version must fix: Un lector espera una preferencia clara y a continuación una razón, pero la frase siguiente dice que no sabe cuál es mejor, así que se contradice. No queda claro qué decisión toma el autor.
Reference version: "Primero, prefiero una habitación en casa de una familia de acogida y no un piso compartido, porque así aprendo más español."
Also fine: "Primero, quiero alojarme con una familia de acogida y no en un piso compartido, porque así aprendo más."; "Primero, prefiero vivir con una familia de acogida en lugar de en un piso compartido, para aprender más español."
Likely mistakes, numbered:
1. The sentence still hedges or says he does not know which option is better, so the preference is unclear.
2. The phrase 'con familia' is carried over from English 'with family' and does not sound natural.
3. The term for a host family is in the wrong order or uses 'acogida' as a modifier before 'familia'.
4. The reason for choosing family is missing or stated vaguely.
Choices in the reference, numbered, each with the reason the tutor gave for it:
1. prefiero: Expresa una decisión clara. «No sé cuál es mejor» diría que no ha decidido, y el lector no sabría qué quiere.
2. en casa de una familia de acogida: «Con familia» es una calca del inglés. Para vivir en la casa de alguien se dice «en casa de».
3. familia de acogida: Es el término fijo: «familia de acogida», con «de» y el orden familia–acogida. «Acogida familia» no funciona como adjetivo.
4. y no un piso compartido: Deja claro qué no quiere. Así la pregunta siguiente sobre «el piso» tiene sentido.
5. porque así aprendo más español: Da la razón en forma de decisión. «Para aprender» sirve, pero «porque así aprendo más» deja claro que la familia le ayuda más.
The learner's new version: "Primero, prefiero una habitación en casa de una familia de acogida y no un piso compartido, porque así aprendo más español."
The post with it in place:
<<<
Estimada Sra. Morales:

Mi nombre es Daniel y yo soy de Manchester, en Inglaterra. Le escribo porque quiero inscribirme en el curso de septiembre. Vengo por mejorar mi español: mi novia es de Granada, conocí a su familia el año pasado pero no entendí casi nada, y estoy muy excitado de aprender para poder hablar con ellos.

¿Es posible que usted me envíe información sobre los precios? También tengo algunas preguntas. Primero, prefiero una habitación en casa de una familia de acogida y no un piso compartido, porque así aprendo más español. ¿Es el piso cerca de la escuela? Necesito una habitación tranquila para estudiar. Segundo, ¿puedo traer mi bicicleta? Me gusta montar en bici y quiero explorar las montañas. Tercero, soy vegetariano (I'm not picky but I don't eat meat) y espero que la familia pueda cocinar algo para mí. Mi novia viene conmigo el primer fin de semana.

¿Me puedes decir cuándo empiezan los cursos? Necesito una respuesta antes de fin de mes porque tengo que comprar el vuelo. Estoy seguro de que voy a pasarlo muy bien en su escuela. Mirando adelante a oír de usted.

Saludos,
Daniel Clarke
>>>

Rules:
- verdict "pass" when a fluent reader would take away the writer's meaning (nothing missing, nothing added that changes it) and nothing in the new version is wrong or unnatural enough that a careful native editor would change it. Matters of taste are not errors. Otherwise "retry".
- A tense that does not fit the surrounding post (present in a past narrative, or the reverse) is an error.
- A word that says something other than what the writer means is an error even when it is fluent (a near-synonym with another sense, a pronoun whose referent becomes unclear).
- Sentence-final punctuation is placed automatically when the version goes into the post: whether the learner typed a full stop (or other final mark) at the very end is never an error and never a reason to retry.
- errors: only real Spanish errors in the new version (grammar, wrong word, a structure carried over from English), each with the exact words, the fix, and why (the why always in Spanish). Not differences from the reference.
- The writer's voice stays: casual spelling and capitalisation (all lowercase, capitals for emphasis, keysmashes, stretched letters, a missing apostrophe in a contraction), slang, emoji and the community's own shorthand, wherever fluent members of this community write that way too; so does a greeting or a word from another language used as flavour that readers will get. Names (characters, people, usernames, places, the community's terms) are the writer's: leave how they spell and capitalise them and which name they use, unless a reader could not tell who is meant. None of these is a problem in either pass. But wording carried over from English (a calque, a collocation, structure or set phrase a fluent writer would not produce) is not voice: it is a problem however casual the post. Never count those as errors.
- check: the number of the most important likely mistake the new version makes, or null.
- other: when something is missing or wrong and no numbered mistake fits, describe the problem: problem (English), reader (optional, one Spanish line in character, only when the meaning suffers), hint (Spanish: points at the gap without giving the words), tell (Spanish: the fix plainly). Else null.
- ticks: numbers of the reference's choices the new version also makes, or makes an equally good equivalent of.
- own: when the learner made a good choice of their own that differs from the reference, one Spanish sentence saying why it works; else null.
- choices: one entry per numbered choice of the reference, in order: n; mine: the learner's exact words doing the same job, or null if their version does not do it; verdict: "same" (they made this choice, or one no reader would tell apart: two coordinated words in another order, an article, a contraction, a synonym with no difference here), "also" (a different choice that is just as right here), "needed" (a different choice, and the reference's is needed). The tutor's reasons are claims, not facts: "needed" only when the reason really holds for their words; when it does not (their words are not wrong or unnatural here), the verdict is "also", "missing" (their version does not do this job); note: only for "also" and "needed", in Spanish, one or two sentences on what their words say or imply here next to the reference's, so they see exactly how the two differ (for "needed", why the reference's choice is needed). Do not repeat the reason the tutor gave; add only what is about their words. When the reason criticised words they kept and it does not hold, the note says so plainly.
- extra: other places where their version differs from the reference in a way worth a word and no numbered choice covers it (at most two): mine, ref (the reference's words for the same job), ok, note (Spanish, as above). Never a difference no reader would notice. [] if none.
- tutor: null when nothing above is a problem. Otherwise what the tutor says to the learner now, in Spanish, addressing them informally, at most two sentences: quote their exact words that need work and say concretely what a reader takes from them versus what they mean (or what is missing, naming the idea, not the Spanish words). This is try number 1: point at the problem without giving the replacement words. Never repeat what the tutor already said to them; never generic advice like "check your meaning".
- repaired: null when nothing above is a problem. Otherwise their version with the smallest changes that fix every problem above: keep their words, word order and structure wherever they work; add what is missing in the same style. It covers exactly the stretch their version covers: never copy in text from the post before or after it.
- The writer may write to you in any language; whatever they write in, everything you write for them is in Spanish.

First write reads_as: in English, what a reader takes this new version to say, as they would understand it in the post.
Then missing: the parts of the writer's meaning, or of what the original part said and the reference keeps, that the new version leaves out (short English phrases; [] if none). Count meaning, not words: dropping a word that does not change what a reader takes away is fine. If the original's problem was that something was only implied, it is still missing while it is only implied.
Then hits: for each numbered likely mistake, in order, true if the new version makes it.
Then errors, other, choices, extra, tutor and repaired as above; there is no verdict field and no ticks field.

Reply with JSON only, fields in this order: {"reads_as":"","missing":[],"hits":[false,false,false,false],"meaning_ok":true,"errors":[{"words":"","fix":"","why":""}],"check":null,"other":null,"choices":[{"n":1,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":2,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":3,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":4,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null},{"n":5,"mine":null,"verdict":"same","note":null}],"extra":[],"tutor":null,"repaired":null}
Each extra item, if any, is {"mine":"","ref":"","ok":true,"note":""}.
